question: May a non-compliant experimental traffic control device be used on a street open to public travel before FHWA approval to experiment is received?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. A non-compliant experimental device is prohibited on any street, highway, bikeway, or site roadway open to public travel until official FHWA approval to experiment has been received. This flows from the broader federal requirement that devices on roads open to public travel substantially conform to FHWA-issued or -endorsed Standards. Standards (mandatory): - "A traffic control device or application that does not comply with the provisions of this Manual shall not be used on any street, highway, bikeway, or site roadway open to public travel (see definition in Section 1C.02) without first receiving official approval to experiment from the FHWA's Office of Transportation Operations." - "The U.S. Secretary of Transportation, under authority granted by the Highway Safety Act of 1966, decreed that traffic control devices on all streets and highways open to public travel in accordance with 23 U.S.C. 109(d) and 402(a) in each State shall be in substantial conformance with the Standards issued or endorsed by the FHWA." - "Before any highway, site roadway open to public travel (see definition in Section 1C.02), detour, or temporary route is opened to public travel, all traffic control devices necessary for safe operation shall be in place." Citations: - Section 1B.05 Standard §2 (p.6) - Section 1B.03 Standard §1 (p.5) - Section 1D.09 Standard §1 (p.38)
gold_answer: No. A non-compliant device or application may not be used on a covered public-travel facility without first receiving official experimentation approval from the FHWA Office of Transportation Operations.
